Finally, we wish for all and every Rural Dean of our Diocese of Constance to be seriously admonished that, beyond this annual visitation, they should nevertheless diligently superintend and solicitously keep watch at all times as to whether those things that have been decreed and defined in the Council of Trent and in the Synodal Statutes are correctly carried into execution. Saint-Cyran seized this occasion to declaim against the regulars and issued that famous pamphlet on the *Hierarchy* under the feigned name of *Petrus Aurelius*. The work pleased as long as the Author remained hidden, and was approved by the Synod of the Gallican Clergy on the 27th of April, 1641, and was committed to the press at their expense. The Bishop of Grasse, Godeau, added an eulogy, in which the author is proclaimed "the most invincible defender of Bishops, the most keen lover of truth, the most just vindicator of the Hierarchy, a Theologian raised in the bosom of ancestral Theology." Saint-Cyran's modesty did not have enough strength so that he might prefer to remain hidden longer amidst such commendation of himself and his labor. But when the Author was discovered, a blush seized his face, and all that pomposity of words finally vanished even from the book: *Gallia Christiana*.

Indeed, he proved himself a Candidate of ancestral Theology in the book condemned on the 23rd of April, 1654: *Familiar Theology, or a brief explanation of the mysteries of the faith*.

…ence, complaints and various pamphlets, two of which were accused of carping at the episcopal authority, certainly of deferring less to the same. Saint-Cyran seized this occasion to declaim against the Regulars, and issued that famous pamphlet on the *Hierarchy* under the assumed name of *Petrus Aurelius*. The work pleased as long as the Author lay hidden, and it was approved by the Synod of the Gallican Clergy on April 27, 1641, and committed to the press at their expense. Godeau, Bishop of Grasse, added an eulogy, in which the author is heralded as "the most invincible defender of Bishops, the most acerbic lover of truth, the most just avenger of the Hierarchy, a theologian educated in the bosom of ancestral theology." The modesty of Saint-Cyran did not have enough strength so that, in such great commendation of himself and his labor, he would prefer to lie hidden longer. But with the Author discovered, a blush invaded his face, and all that pomp of words finally vanished even from the book: *Gallia Christiana* .

He certainly proved himself a Candidate of ancestral theology in the book condemned on April 23, 1654: *Theologia Familiaris, seu brevis explicatio mysteriorum Fidei* .

### On the seven theological and cardinal virtues.

Ninth, I sinned by omission, because I neglected to keep the three theological virtues and the four cardinal ones. In me, there is not the true faith of Christ with good works. …Hence there were complaints and various pamphlets, two of which were accused of carping at episcopal authority, or certainly of deferring too little to it. Sancyranus gladly seized this occasion to declaim against the Regulars, and he issued that famous pamphlet on the *Hierarchy* under the false name of *Petrus Aurelius*. The work pleased as long as the author remained hidden, and it was approved by the Synod of the Gallican Clergy on April 27, 1641, and committed to the press at their expense. Godeau, Bishop of Grasse, added a eulogy in which the author is proclaimed "the most invincible defender of Bishops, the keenest lover of truth, the most just vindicator of the Hierarchy, a theologian educated in the bosom of ancestral Theology." The modesty of Sancyranus did not have enough strength to prefer remaining hidden for long in such commendation of himself and his labor. But once the Author was discovered, a blush invaded his face, and all that pomp of words finally vanished even from the book: *Gallia Christiana*.

Indeed, he proved himself a candidate of ancestral Theology in the book condemned on April 23, 1654: *Theologia Familiaris, seu brevis explicatio mysteriorum Fidei* .

What, then? Is God distinct from the Persons? Further, he says "The Church is the Society of those who serve God in the light and profession of the true faith, in the union of charity." But sinners do not have charity: are they, therefore, not of the Church?

To pass over other rags, the Treatise of Augustine on Virginity, which he had edited with notes in the French idiom under the name of P. Seguenot, Priest of the Oratory, was fatal to him. Because of this, and also because he was now restraining himself less, he was arrested by order of Cardinal Richelieu along with Seguenot, and thrown into prison in the same year and month that Jansenius had died, on May 14. Released from there after the death of the Cardinal, without causing any further disturbance, he was shortly thereafter struck by an apoplexy and departed to the majority on October 11, 1643.
